evidence.dominant_driver: UK headline CPI rose to 3.1% y/y as expected, driven mainly by motor fuels, while core CPI stayed 2.6% and services inflation 3.4%.

market_expectations.distribution_notes: BoE hold is still the base case; market reports around 80% hold probability.

absorption.reason: Headline and core matched consensus; UK cash equities had not opened yet, but rates already carried a substantial inflation premium and GBP weakened slightly after the release.

observations.GBP: slightly weaker, not a hawkish confirmation

evidence.decision_notes: Residual forecast from 06:49:45Z; UK100 cash market not yet open, so fixed 15m/1h horizons are not substituted with the later market open. No M2 ACTIONABLE learning segment was used to alter confidence.

immediate.rationale: CPI matched consensus and UK cash market is still closed; no clean residual directional edge.

next_session.rationale: BoE decision and global rates should dominate after the initial inflation read.

15m.rationale: Cash market closed; headline/core matched consensus and GBP reaction is not hawkish.

1h.rationale: Near the London open, high gilt yields conflict with a largely expected, energy-led CPI rise.

4h.rationale: Stable core/services inflation offsets the headline acceleration; BoE hold remains base case.

next_session.rationale: BoE decision and Fed spillover dominate the next session.

predictions.mechanism: Expected headline inflation rise increases nominal-rate pressure, but stable core/services and weaker GBP limit a clean bearish equity signal.
predictions.invalidation: A sharp gilt-yield rise with broad FTSE selling after the open would validate a bearish path; falling yields plus commodity strength would favor upside.
predictions.counter_case: FTSE 100 can rise if falling oil/yields and its international revenue mix outweigh domestic inflation concerns.

technical_state.source: UK100 cash session status at decision time
